clauses.reason: Sec. 1 is a self-executing amendment: EO 10621 "is hereby amended by adding the following paragraph at the end of Section 1 thereof" (paragraph (o)). It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966; no later effective date appears. The paragraph continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986; EO 12396 (1982) did not revoke paragraph (o). The 1986 revocation is a later event for this clause, not its first end.

Sec. 2 delegates to the Secretary of State the authority vested in the President by Section 3 of the Travel Expense Act of 1949 (5 U.S.C. 836) to establish maximum per diem rates for travel status in areas outside the United States. It is a continuing delegation. EO 12561 Sec. 3 reads "Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4,1966, is revoked." and, in its Sec. 2, delegates to the Secretary of State the successor authority under Section 102(a) of the 1985 Act (5 U.S.C. 5702(a)) for the same areas. The order states no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, July 1, 1986. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 of EO 11294, so Sec. 2 is not shown to have ended earlier.

Sec. 3 is a self-executing amendment of EO 11230: paragraph (9) of Section 1 is substituted by new text delegating the per diem authority for travel outside the 48 contiguous States to the Bureau of the Budget. It was complete on signing, August 4, 1966. EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) then superseded "Section 3 of Executive Order No. 11294 of August 4, 1966" with immediate effect under its Sec. 12 (July 22, 1971), and EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294 on July 1, 1986. Both are later events; they are not the first end of a command that was spent on issue.

Sec. 4 supersedes EO 10970 of October 27, 1961 "To the extent not heretofore superseded". A supersession of another order is complete on issue, August 4, 1966; no later effective date appears. The revocation of EO 11294 in 1986 does not revive EO 10970 and is a later event only.

research_rationale:
EO 11294 (31 FR 10601, signed 1966-08-04) has four sections. Sec. 1 adds paragraph (o) to Section 1 of EO 10621 (per diem delegation to the Secretary of Defense for Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, the Canal Zone and possessions); Sec. 3 substitutes paragraph (9) of Section 1 of EO 11230; Sec. 4 supersedes EO 10970 to the extent not already superseded. Each is a self-executing amendment or supersession spent on signing, 1966-08-04. Sec. 2 is a continuing delegation to the Secretary of State of the President's per diem authority for areas outside the United States; it ended on 1986-07-01 when EO 12561 Sec. 3 revoked EO 11294, in the same order that re-delegated the successor authority to the Secretary of State (Sec. 2) and revoked paragraph (o) of EO 10621 (Sec. 1). EO 11609 Sec. 11(5) superseded only Section 3 on 1971-07-22. The latest clause end, 1986-07-01, is the whole-order end. No held text shows an earlier end of Sec. 2, and the bounded searches found no other instrument naming EO 11294 as amended or revoked.

savings.reason: Paragraph (o) added by Sec. 1 continued inside EO 10621 until EO 12561 Sec. 1 revoked "the current subsection (o)" on 1986-07-01, and paragraph (9) substituted by Sec. 3 continued in EO 11230 until EO 11609 superseded that parent on 1971-07-22; both are consequences in the parent orders, not continuing commands of EO 11294. The Sec. 2 delegation was replaced by the delegation in EO 12561 Sec. 2 under the 1985 Act. Per diem rates fixed under the delegation are accrued results.
